description: We are building an interactive Martian multi-layered navigation map for the NASA Space Apps challenge. We are looking for passionate members skilled in data, design, coding, and strategy to join our innovative team!
summary:
The Martian map is an interactive web based platform designed to help future human explorers and the service reverse negate the surface of Mars safely and efficiently. As NASA and space agencies prepare for crewed missions to the red planet, identifying safe travel routes and avoiding hazardous terrain is essential. Our project addresses this challenge by providing a 3D map that supports route planning through the visualization of Martian terrain and environmental hazards. 

The platform allows users to explore the landscape, select destinations, and find routes between locations. By integrating scientific data from NASA, the system display critical geographic features, including elevation changes, craters, slopes, and rocky terrain. It’s highlights potential hazards and compares routes based on distance, terrain difficulty, and estimated travel time.
A key feature is a 3D route visualization, helping users understand terrain along a proposed journey rather than relying on a flat map. A dedicated dashboard presents route length, elevation profiles, and identified hazards, making complex planetary data easy to interpret. By combining interactive mapping, 3D  visualization, and data-driven route assessment, Martian Map contributes to safer planetary navigation for future missions.
details:
1. Description of the Proposed Solution

Martian Map is an online platform that lets users explore Mars in 3D and plan risk-aware routes for future astronauts and rovers. Steep slopes, craters, and rocky fields can slow a journey or make it dangerous, so explorers need to know the terrain before they move. Our platform shows the landscape, finds routes between two points, and shows the risk level of each route.

2. How Does the Solution Work?

1. Data Collection: We gather open elevation data from NASA and other planetary sources like MOLA and HiRISE to create a height map for one or two selected regions on Mars.

2. 3D Terrain Visualization: This height map is drawn as a 3D surface that users can rotate, zoom, and explore in their browser.

3. Terrain Analysis: We find the slope by measuring height differences between neighboring points, and we estimate rough ground from how much the height changes in small areas. This is an estimate, not a direct count of rocks, and it works best in regions with high-resolution data. Craters are marked using NASA data, and each location is given a difficulty score.

4. Route Planning: Users choose a starting point and a destination. A pathfinding algorithm searches for routes and gives higher costs to difficult ground, so it can compare the shortest route with the lowest-risk one.

5. Route Display and Dashboard: The route is shown on the 3D terrain with colors for difficulty: green for easy, yellow for medium, and red for risky. A dashboard shows the distance, elevation profile, hazards, and estimated travel time, which is calculated from an assumed average speed that gets lower on steep ground.

3. Technologies Used

• HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: for the website interface and the route logic.

• Three.js: a free library that draws the Martian terrain and routes in 3D.

• A* pathfinding algorithm: to find routes based on distance and terrain difficulty.

• NASA planetary datasets: real data for elevation, craters, and surface features.

• Chart.js: to show the elevation profile on the dashboard.

All these tools are free and work in a standard web browser.

4. Feasibility of the Proposed Solution

This project is realistic for a student team. It uses free public data and common web tools, and it needs no special hardware or new satellite observations. We will start with Jezero Crater, the landing site of the Perseverance rover, because high-resolution data is available for it. We will build the platform in stages: 3D terrain first, then terrain analysis, then route planning, and finally the colored hazards and the dashboard.

The main challenges are preparing data from different sources and handling areas with limited information. We will manage them by working on one or two selected regions and testing each stage before moving on. As a prototype, the platform helps with planning but cannot guarantee complete safety, and its results depend on the quality of the data.

5. Innovation and Uniqueness

Many Mars maps focus on viewing the surface. Martian Map focuses on deciding how to cross it.

• Risk-aware routes: Routes are judged by slope, roughness, and hazards instead of distance alone, because the shortest path is not always the safest.

• Visible risks: The colors along the route show exactly where the risk is, so explorers do not need to read raw numbers.

• One place for decisions: Distance, elevation, hazards, and travel time are shown together on one dashboard.

• Open and accessible: It uses open NASA data and runs in any browser, so students and mission planners can try it easily.

This turns complex scientific data into a clear tool that helps future missions make better decisions and avoid unnecessary risks.
